requirements.title: One poll loop per subscribed workspace
requirements.rationale: Labelling an issue must trigger work with no client, without hammering hub or overlapping cycles.

criteria.condition: agent-fox starts
criteria.action: start after the jobs layer has started, read the store's subscriptions, and start exactly one loop per subscribed workspace
criteria.contract: the poll supervisor start is recorded after the jobs layer start; exactly one loop exists for widgets and one for gadgets

setup: a temporary database with subscriptions widgets and gadgets
a recording start hook on the jobs layer and on the poll supervisor
check.pseudocode: start(); assert order.index('poll') > order.index('jobs'); assert loops == {'widgets':1,'gadgets':1}

criteria.condition: a subscription scan, run at start and then every 60 seconds, finds a subscribed workspace that has no loop
criteria.action: start one loop for that workspace, so that no workspace ever has more than one loop
criteria.contract: gadgets gets exactly one loop; widgets still has exactly one loop; the first poll of gadgets happens within one scan period plus the first-cycle delay

setup: the supervisor running with a scan period of 60 s on an injected clock
widgets subscribed and polled
check.pseudocode: subscribe('gadgets'); clock.advance(60s); clock.advance(60s); assert loopCount('gadgets')==1 and loopCount('widgets')==1

criteria.condition: a subscription scan finds that a workspace with a loop is no longer subscribed
criteria.action: stop that workspace's loop and cancel any cycle it has in flight
criteria.contract: after the scan, the fake hub records no further request made with that workspace's PAT

setup: widgets subscribed, a cycle in flight held by a fake hub delay on the list request
check.pseudocode: hub.delay('issues'); startCycle(); store.delete('widgets'); scan(); n=hub.count(pat); clock.advance(1h); assert hub.count(pat)==n

criteria.action: start the workspace's first cycle after a random delay of 0 to 30 seconds, start each later cycle one interval (15-REQ-2) after the previous cycle ended, and never run two cycles of one workspace at the same time
criteria.contract: the first cycle starts at 17 s; each later cycle starts 2 minutes after the previous cycle ended; at most one cycle of widgets is in flight at any time; the default delay source only ever yields values in [0,30s]

setup: a first-cycle delay source returning 17 s
a fake hub whose list request takes 2 minutes of injected clock
AF_POLL_INTERVAL 2m
check.pseudocode: record start/end times; assert start[i+1]-end[i]==2m; assert maxConcurrent==1; for _ in 1000: assert 0<=defaultDelay()<=30s

criteria.condition: four cycles are running across all workspaces
criteria.action: make any further due cycle wait until a running cycle ends and frees a slot
criteria.contract: exactly four variables reads are in flight; the other two wait; when one is released a waiting cycle starts; the in-flight count never exceeds 4

setup: six subscribed workspaces
a fake hub that holds every variables read until released
first-cycle delay zero
check.pseudocode: assert hub.inflight()==4; release(1); wait; assert hub.inflight()==4 and hub.started==5

criteria.condition: a cycle has run for 5 minutes
criteria.action: cancel the cycle, keep every job created, record written and label removed before the cancel, and schedule the next cycle as for a cycle that ended early (15-REQ-2.5)
criteria.contract: the cycle's context is cancelled at 5 minutes of injected clock; its slot is freed

setup: af:triage on issue 7 and af:fix on issue 42
the fake hub answers the fix list only after hanging
the triage job for 7 already created and its label removed
check.pseudocode: clock.advance(5m); assert ctx.err==Canceled; assert jobs.count==1; assert slots.free==4; assert nextStart==now+lastInterval

criteria.condition: agent-fox begins shutdown
criteria.action: start no new cycle, cancel the cycles in flight, and return before the jobs layer begins its own shutdown
criteria.contract: the poll's stop call returns before the jobs layer's stop is called

setup: a cycle in flight held on hub
recording stop hooks on the poll and on the jobs layer
check.pseudocode: shutdown(); assert order==['poll.stop returned','jobs.stop called']; clock.advance(1h); assert hub.count()==before

criteria.action: accept an injected clock, first-cycle delay, subscription scan period and hold release delay, defaulting to the wall clock, a random 0-30 s delay, 60 s and 5 minutes
criteria.contract: defaults are wall clock, a delay in [0,30s], scan period 60 s, release delay 5 minutes; injected values replace each default

setup: a supervisor built with no options
a supervisor built with injected clock, delay, scan period and release delay
check.pseudocode: d=New(); assert d.scan==60s and d.release==5m and d.clock is time.Now; i=New(opts); assert i.scan==injected

requirements.title: The interval and the label prefix
requirements.rationale: AF_POLL_INTERVAL is the poll's only setting and bounds the forge rate limit it spends; the subscription prefix keeps the poll and the worker in agreement.

criteria.condition: a cycle reads the workspace's resolved hub variables and `AF_POLL_INTERVAL` is unset or empty
criteria.action: use an interval of 5 minutes
criteria.contract: with the variable unset, list requests are 5 minutes apart; after the change to 2m, list requests are 2 minutes apart; 24h is accepted as 24h and 1m as 1m

setup: workspace widgets with AF_POLL_INTERVAL unset on the fake hub
check.pseudocode: gaps=diff(hub.listTimes()); assert all(g==5m); hub.setVar('AF_POLL_INTERVAL','2m'); ...assert all(g==2m)

criteria.condition: a cycle reads `AF_POLL_INTERVAL` as a zero duration (`0`, `0s`, `0m`)
criteria.action: end the cycle right after the variables read without reading the workspace record, listing issues or writing a label, and start the next cycle 5 minutes later
criteria.contract: across 30 minutes of injected clock the fake hub records no list request and one variables read every 5 minutes

setup: AF_POLL_INTERVAL set to 0 (also 0s and 0m in turn)
issues labelled af:triage and af:fix exist
check.pseudocode: assert hub.count('issues')==0 and hub.count('workspace')==0; assert gaps(hub.varReads)==5m; hub.setVar('1m'); advance(5m); assert hub.count('issues')>0

criteria.condition: a cycle reads `AF_POLL_INTERVAL` as a Go duration from `1m` to `24h` inclusive
criteria.action: use that duration as the interval

criteria.condition: `AF_POLL_INTERVAL` is unparsable, negative, below `1m` or above `24h`
criteria.action: use an interval of 5 minutes and log a `WARN` record naming the workspace, the variable and the value, once per distinct value
criteria.contract: exactly one WARN record per distinct invalid value; list requests 5 minutes apart

setup: a captured slog handler
values 30s, abc, -1m and 25h set in turn, each across several cycles
check.pseudocode: for v in ['30s','abc','-1m','25h']: set(v); run 3 cycles; assert warns(v)==1 and gaps==5m

criteria.condition: a cycle ends before it could read `AF_POLL_INTERVAL`
criteria.action: start the next cycle after the interval the workspace last read, or after 5 minutes when the last value read disabled the poll or none has been read
criteria.contract: after 2m was read, the next cycle starts 2 minutes after the failed one; after 0 was read, the next cycle starts 5 minutes later; with none read, the next cycle starts 5 minutes later

setup: AF_POLL_INTERVAL 2m read in one cycle
then the variables read answers 503
check.pseudocode: assert nextStart(after_2m)==end+2m; assert nextStart(after_0)==end+5m; assert nextStart(none)==end+5m

criteria.action: name the request labels `<prefix>triage` and `<prefix>fix` from the subscription's `label_prefix` read from the store at the start of each cycle, and never use `AF_LABEL_PREFIX` to name them
criteria.contract: the first cycle lists af:triage then af:fix; the second cycle lists ci:triage then ci:fix; no list ever uses the other: prefix

setup: widgets subscribed with prefix af:
AF_LABEL_PREFIX set to other: on the hub
check.pseudocode: assert hub.listLabels(cycle1)==['af:triage','af:fix']; store.setPrefix('ci:'); assert hub.listLabels(cycle2)==['ci:triage','ci:fix']

criteria.condition: `AF_LABEL_PREFIX` is set and differs from the subscription's `label_prefix`
criteria.action: keep using the subscription's prefix and log a `WARN` record once per distinct value
criteria.contract: one WARN record per distinct differing value

setup: subscription prefix af:
a captured slog handler
check.pseudocode: assert warns('x:')==1 and warns('y:')==1 and warns('af:')==0

requirements.title: ListIssues in the hub forge client and the fake hub
requirements.rationale: agent_fox_worker left ListIssues unavailable; the poll needs it, with hub's names kept inside internal/hub.

criteria.condition: ListIssues is called with a filter holding `State: "open"`, exactly one label and a `Limit`
criteria.action: send `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues?state=open&labels=<query-escaped label>` with the PAT as bearer token, asking for pages of 100 and sending no sort parameter
criteria.contract: returns issuex.IssueList with the issues in hub's order

setup: the fake hub with workspace widgets and a PAT
a hub forge client bound to widgets
check.pseudocode: list=c.ListIssues(ctx,repo,Filter{State:'open',Labels:['af:fix'],Limit:100}); r=hub.last(); assert r.query=='state=open&labels=af%3Afix' (plus page size) and 'sort' not in r.query

criteria.action: follow hub's further pages until it holds `Limit` issues or hub reports no further page, treating a page whose answer says nothing about further pages as the last
criteria.contract: Limit 100 returns 100 issues and Incomplete true; Limit 250 returns 250 issues and Incomplete false when hub reports no further page; Limit 300 returns 250 issues and Incomplete false; a page whose answer says nothing about further pages is treated as last

setup: the fake hub with 250 open issues under af:fix paged by 100
another listing whose last page says nothing about further pages
check.pseudocode: assert (len(l100.Issues),l100.Incomplete)==(100,True); assert (len(l250.Issues),l250.Incomplete)==(250,False)

criteria.action: set `Incomplete` to true only when it stopped at `Limit` while hub reported a further page
criteria.contract: IssueList.Incomplete

criteria.action: leave out of the returned list every item that hub marks as a pull or merge request
criteria.contract: only issue 5 is returned

setup: fake hub issues 5 (issue), 6 (pull request) and 7 (merge request), all labelled af:fix
check.pseudocode: assert [i.Number for i in list.Issues]==[5]

criteria.condition: the filter sets any other field (Assignee, Sort, Direction, a state other than open, or a label count other than one)
criteria.action: send no request and return the client's "not available through hub" error
criteria.contract: non-nil error; the fake hub records no request

setup: a hub forge client and the fake hub
check.pseudocode: for f in bad_filters: err=c.ListIssues(ctx,repo,f); assert err!=nil and 'not available through hub' in err.Error(); assert hub.requests()==[]

criteria.condition: hub answers a list page with an error
criteria.action: map the answer as for the client's other forge methods: 401/403 to *issuex.HTTPError, 404 to not found, 409 to issuex's conflict error, another 4xx to a rejected error carrying hub's message, 429 to rate-limited, and 5xx, transport errors, timeouts and bodies that are not the expected JSON to a retryable error
criteria.contract: the returned error satisfies the matching issuex predicate (IsNotFound, IsRateLimited, ...)

setup: the fake hub answering the list with each status in turn
check.pseudocode: table of (status, predicate); assert predicate(err) for each

criteria.action: keep hub's route, field names, paging and pull-request marker inside `internal/hub`, and no longer list ListIssues among the unavailable methods
criteria.contract: no package outside internal/hub and its fake mentions them; ListIssues is not in the unavailable-method list; other unavailable methods still send nothing

setup: the source tree and the hub forge client's unavailable-method test
check.pseudocode: assert not grep(hubNames, excluding 'internal/hub'); assert 'ListIssues' not in unavailableMethods

criteria.action: serve the issues-list route from its issue state with the `state` and `labels` filters, paging that can report a further page, issues that are pull requests, a removal lag (an issue stays listed under a label for a set number of lists after its removal) and an addition lag (an issue is left out of a label's lists for a set number of lists after the label was added)
criteria.contract: state and labels filters narrow the result; paging reports a further page when more remain; pull requests are returned with the marker; after removal with lag 2 the issue is still listed under the label for two lists then disappears; after addition with lag 2 the issue is left out of the label's lists for two lists then appears

setup: the fake hub with open and closed issues, a pull request, and 150 issues under one label
check.pseudocode: hub.removalLag(2); remove(42,'af:fix'); assert 42 in list() twice then not in list()

requirements.title: One cycle
requirements.rationale: A fixed, deterministic order per cycle makes the poll testable and queues triage before fix.

criteria.action: in order: bring the workspace's poll records up to date with their jobs (15-REQ-6.4) with no hub request, read the subscription's label prefix and PAT from the store, read the workspace's resolved hub variables with the PAT, and, when enabled, read the workspace record for the forge repository and list `<prefix>triage` then `<prefix>fix`, each with a limit of 100
criteria.contract: the fake hub records the variables read, the workspace record read, the triage list and the fix list in that order

setup: widgets subscribed, polling enabled
check.pseudocode: assert hub.paths()==['vars','workspace','issues(af:triage)','issues(af:fix)']

criteria.action: take each listing's issues in ascending issue number, whatever order hub returned, and apply 15-REQ-5 to each
criteria.contract: with af:triage on 7 and af:fix on 42, the triage job for 7 is created before the fix job for 42

setup: the real jobs layer with the fake runner on a temporary database
check.pseudocode: for nums,perm in gen(): hub.setOrder(perm); cycle(); assert created==sorted(triageNums)+sorted(fixNums)

criteria.condition: a listing of a label comes back with `Incomplete` true
criteria.action: log a `WARN` record naming the workspace and the label, and not again for that label until a listing of it has come back complete
criteria.contract: three incomplete listings in a row produce exactly one WARN record

setup: af:fix listing that is always incomplete (more than 100 issues)
a captured slog handler
check.pseudocode: assert warns('af:fix')==1 after 3 cycles; ...==2 after the later incomplete one

criteria.condition: a listing is incomplete
criteria.action: release no hold and settle no owed removal on the basis of that listing, leaving issues past its last page to a later cycle
criteria.contract: the hold on 42 is still in place; the owed removal for 43 is still owed; a later complete listing without them releases and settles both

setup: a held label on 42 whose release delay has elapsed
an owed removal for issue 43
an incomplete af:fix listing that contains neither 42 nor 43
check.pseudocode: assert rec(42).hold and rec(43).owed after incomplete; after complete: assert not rec(42).hold and not rec(43).owed

criteria.action: for any issue that is closed, is a pull request, or carries neither request label, create no job and send no label removal for it
criteria.contract: no job is created; the fake hub records no label removal; the labels remain on all three

setup: pull request 3 with af:fix
closed issue 4 with af:triage
open issue 5 labelled bug
check.pseudocode: assert jobs.count()==0 and hub.removals()==[]

criteria.condition: a cycle runs and `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` for its workspace starts at the same time
criteria.action: create no job for that workspace
criteria.contract: the jobs table holds no job for the workspace created by the poll after DELETE began

setup: af:fix on issue 42 and the real API and jobs layer
the cycle held just before job creation
check.pseudocode: hold; go delete(); release; assert not any(j.created_at>deleteStart)

criteria.action: never write a PAT into any log record or any job field
criteria.contract: no captured log record and no job row contains the PAT string

setup: widgets with a distinctive PAT
a captured slog handler
scenarios with success, 403, 503, 409 and an unreadable token
check.pseudocode: assert pat not in logs and pat not in dump(af_jobs)

requirements.title: What a listed issue becomes
requirements.rationale: Each labelled request must become exactly one job, and a second request while one runs must be absorbed.

criteria.condition: issue N is listed under label L of kind K and the jobs layer has an open (queued, running or blocked) job of kind K for N on the workspace
criteria.action: remove L from N (15-REQ-6), create no job, and log the absorbed label at `INFO` with the workspace, kind, issue and job id; an open job of the other kind does not absorb L
criteria.contract: the job count is unchanged; the fake hub records one removal of L from N

setup: fix job for 42 created through the API and running
af:fix added to 42
an open triage job for 42 and af:fix on 42 in a second scenario
a blocked fix job for 42 in a third scenario
check.pseudocode: assert jobs.count()==before and hub.removals('af:fix',42)==1 and info_absorbed(job.id)

criteria.condition: the removal of an absorbed label fails
criteria.action: write a poll record for N and L with the removal owed and no job
criteria.contract: a later cycle that lists N under L after the open job ended removes L and creates no job

setup: running API fix job for 42
af:fix added to 42
the removal of af:fix from 42 answers 503
check.pseudocode: assert rec.job is None and rec.owed; end job; cycle(); assert removed and jobs.count()==1; cycle(); assert jobs.count()==1

criteria.condition: issue N is listed under label L, no open job of kind K absorbs it, and a hold on L for N is in place (15-REQ-7)
criteria.action: leave L on N, create no job and send no removal
criteria.contract: no job is created; no removal of af:fix is sent; the label stays on 42

setup: a hold on af:fix for 42 in place
check.pseudocode: assert jobs.count()==before and hub.removals()==[]

criteria.condition: issue N is listed under label L, neither absorbed nor held, and a removal of L from N is owed
criteria.action: remove L from N and create no job
criteria.contract: the job count is unchanged

setup: a record for 42 and af:fix with the removal owed, its job done
the fake hub lists 42 under af:fix
check.pseudocode: cycle(); assert hub.removals('af:fix',42)==1 and jobs.count()==1

criteria.condition: issue N is listed under label L of kind K and none of rules absorbed, held or already taken applies (a failed job is not open)
criteria.action: create a job through the jobs layer's entry point with kind K, input `{issue: N}`, source `{kind: "label", by: "label <L>"}` and request label L, log it at `INFO` with the workspace, kind, issue and job id, and then consume L (15-REQ-6)
criteria.contract: the job's source is {kind: "label", by: "label af:fix"} for L = af:fix and its request_label is L; the fake hub records the removal after the job exists

setup: open issue 7 with af:triage and open issue 42 with af:fix
the real jobs layer with the fake runner
check.pseudocode: assert job7.source=={'kind':'label','by':'label af:triage'} and job7.request_label=='af:triage'; assert hub.removalTime(7)>job7.created; cycle(); assert jobs.count()==2

criteria.condition: the jobs entry point refuses with a duplicate because a job for the same workspace, kind and issue was created in the meantime
criteria.action: handle the issue as absorbed (15-REQ-5.1, 15-REQ-5.2)
criteria.contract: exactly one job for the workspace, kind and issue exists; L is removed or recorded as owed

setup: the entry point refuses with duplicate because an API job for 42 appeared after the open-job check
check.pseudocode: assert count(jobs, kind='fix', issue=42)==1 and (hub.removed or rec.owed)

criteria.condition: the jobs entry point refuses with not subscribed
criteria.action: end the cycle at once and write no label
criteria.contract: no further hub request in the cycle

setup: af:triage on 7 and af:fix on 42
the jobs entry point refuses the first create with not subscribed
check.pseudocode: assert hub.requestsAfter(refusal)==[] and hub.removals()==[]

criteria.condition: the jobs entry point refuses with token unreadable or returns any other error
criteria.action: log a `WARN` record, leave L on the issue, and end the cycle
criteria.contract: no removal of L is sent; one WARN record

setup: af:triage on 7 and af:fix on 42
the entry point returns token unreadable, then another error in a second scenario
check.pseudocode: assert hub.removals()==[] and warns()==1 and jobs.count()==0

requirements.title: Consuming the label and the poll's records
requirements.rationale: A durable record of owed removals and job observations stops a failed removal or a purged job from turning one label into two jobs.

criteria.action: keep poll records in a table `af_poll_requests` created by a migration appended to the core's `af_` migration list, with no foreign key to `af_jobs`, so that records survive a restart and the retention purge of their job
criteria.contract: table af_poll_requests exists; PRAGMA foreign_key_list(af_poll_requests) is empty; the new migration is the last entry and earlier entries are unchanged; records survive reopening the database file

setup: a fresh database migrated by the store
check.pseudocode: assert fk_list=='[]'; write rec; reopen(); assert rec exists

criteria.condition: the poll creates a job
criteria.action: write a poll record right after the job is created and before the removal, carrying the workspace, the issue, the label, the job id, an owed flag and what the poll has seen of the job
criteria.contract: at the time of the removal request, a record for widgets, 42, af:fix carries the job id and the removal owed; after success the owed flag is cleared

setup: af:fix on 42
a hook on the fake hub that reads the poll table when the removal arrives
check.pseudocode: hub.onRemove=lambda: snapshot=rec(); assert snapshot.job_id==job.id and snapshot.owed

criteria.condition: a poll record cannot be written
criteria.action: log a `WARN` record and still send the label removal
criteria.contract: one WARN record; the removal request is recorded by the fake hub

setup: af:fix on 42
the poll table's writes fail
check.pseudocode: breakTable(); cycle(); assert warns()==1 and hub.removals('af:fix',42)==1

criteria.condition: a cycle starts, before any hub request and whether or not the poll turns out to be enabled
criteria.action: read the job of each of the workspace's records whose job it has not yet seen end, and note: a `done` job, or a `cancelled` job without a hold, as ended holding nothing; a holding job, and the first time no runner of it is in progress; a job that is gone (purged) as holding from the moment it was found gone; and a `queued`, `running`, `blocked` or `failed` job as not ended
criteria.contract: reconciliation happened before the first hub request; done and cancelled-without-hold records are marked ended holding nothing; the cancelled-with-hold record has its release clock started at the first time no runner is in progress; the purged record holds from the moment found gone; queued, running, blocked and failed records are not ended

setup: records for jobs that are done, cancelled without a hold, cancelled with a hold and no runner left, purged, queued, running, blocked and failed
AF_POLL_INTERVAL 0
check.pseudocode: reconcile(); assert state(rec_done)=='ended' ... assert rec_purged.hold and rec_purged.clock==now; assert state(rec_failed)=='open'

criteria.condition: a removal of L from N succeeds or hub answers it with not found (404)
criteria.action: confirm every owed removal recorded for N and L, logging no failure for the 404
criteria.contract: no failure record; the owed flags for N and L are cleared

setup: two owed records for 42 and af:fix
hub answers the removal with 404 in one scenario and 200 in another
check.pseudocode: hub.removeAnswer(404); cycle(); assert owed(42,'af:fix')==0 and failures()==[]

criteria.condition: a removal of L from N fails in any way other than not found
criteria.action: leave the removal owed, keep any job already created, retry the removal whenever N is listed under L, and continue or end the cycle as 15-REQ-8 says
criteria.contract: the created job stands; the next cycle listing N under L removes L and creates no job

setup: the removal of af:fix from 42 answers 503
the fake runner finishes the job to done before the next cycle
check.pseudocode: assert jobs==1; cycle(); assert jobs==1 and removed; cycle(); assert jobs==1; hub.add(42,'af:fix'); cycle(); assert jobs==2

criteria.condition: a complete listing of L does not contain N
criteria.action: settle every owed removal for N and L
criteria.contract: the owed removals are settled; a later af:fix label on 42 makes a new job

setup: owed removals for 42 and af:fix, a person removed the label by hand
check.pseudocode: cycle(); assert owed(42)==0; hub.add(42); cycle(); assert jobs.count()==before+1

criteria.action: drop a record once nothing is owed and nothing holds: its removal has been confirmed or settled and either its job ended holding nothing, its hold was released, or it has no job
criteria.contract: the confirmed done-job, released-hold and confirmed no-job records are gone; the owed record and the open-job record remain

setup: records: owed removal with done job; confirmed with open job; confirmed with done job; confirmed with released hold; no-job record confirmed
check.pseudocode: assert ids(records)=={owed_id, open_id}

requirements.title: A label the service put back
requirements.rationale: Without a hold, a request label the worker restores on cancel would become a new job and the cancel would spend again.

criteria.action: treat a poll-created job as holding its request label from the moment it is cancelled while one of its attempts is in a runner (a cancel caused by an unsubscribe included), whatever the runner later reports, including when the runner overruns the cancel grace and the jobs layer drops its report
criteria.contract: the record holds from the cancel in every scenario; no job for 42 is created and af:fix stays on 42

setup: a poll-created fix job for 42 held by the fake runner
scenarios: runner returns reporting af:fix set; runner overruns the 60 s grace and the report is dropped; cancel caused by unsubscribe
check.pseudocode: cancel(job); hub.add(42,'af:fix'); cycle(); assert holds(rec) and jobs.count()==1

criteria.condition: a hold on L for N is in place
criteria.action: create no job for N and send no removal of L when a listing of L contains N
criteria.contract: across the following cycles, before and after the runner returns and after a restart on the same database file, no job for N is created and L stays on N

setup: a poll-created fix job cancelled while the fake runner holds the attempt
af:fix put back on 42 before the runner returns
check.pseudocode: for c in cycles: cycle(); assert jobs.count('fix',42)==1 and hub.removals('af:fix',42)==1 (the original consumption only)

criteria.action: start a hold's release clock when the poll first sees that no runner of the held job is in progress, or, for a job purged before the poll saw it end, when the poll found it gone
criteria.contract: no release clock before the runner returns; the clock equals the first cycle time that saw no runner in progress; for the purged job the clock equals the time it was found gone

setup: a held job whose runner returns at T
a held job purged before the poll saw it end, found gone at T2
a recording clock
check.pseudocode: assert rec.clock is None; runner.return(); cycle(); assert rec.clock==clock.now()

criteria.condition: a complete listing of L that does not contain N was requested at least the release delay (5 minutes) after the hold's release clock started
criteria.action: release the hold, so that L on N is a request again at a later listing
criteria.contract: after a manual removal and such a listing, adding L again makes exactly one new job

setup: a hold with the release clock started
af:fix removed from 42 by hand
check.pseudocode: hub.remove(42); clock.advance(5m); cycle(); assert not hold; hub.add(42); cycle(); assert jobs.count('fix',42)==2

criteria.condition: a listing of L without N was requested less than the release delay after the release clock started, or is incomplete
criteria.action: keep the hold in place
criteria.contract: with an addition lag of two lists and an interval of 1m, none of the three cycles after the runner returned creates a job or removes L

setup: AF_POLL_INTERVAL 1m
a cancelled poll-created fix job for 42, runner returned
the fake hub leaves af:fix on 42 out of the next two lists
check.pseudocode: hub.additionLag(2); for i in 3: cycle(); assert jobs.count('fix',42)==1 and no removal

criteria.action: treat a job cancelled while queued, while waiting out a transient backoff, or while blocked as holding nothing
criteria.contract: adding its label again makes one new job at the next cycle

setup: poll-created jobs cancelled while queued, while waiting out a transient backoff, and while blocked
check.pseudocode: cancel(queuedJob); hub.add(n,'af:fix'); cycle(); assert jobs.count('fix',n)==2

criteria.action: keep a hold until it is released, across restarts and across the retention purge of its job
criteria.contract: after retention purges the cancelled job, the next three cycles create no job for N and leave L in place

runs the next cycle, finds no labelled issue and creates no job
